Refuse a renv snapshot taken from the wrong R

Source: R/snapshot-guard.R
guard_snapshot.Rd

Stops before renv::snapshot() when the R running this session has a different major.minor version than the R recorded in the study's renv.lock. A snapshot from the wrong R rewrites the lockfile's R version and drops every locked package the session's library lacks. On 2026-10-22, R 4.6.1 snapshotted a study locked to R 4.5.3, and boostmtree and ggBoostedTrees fell out of its lockfile.

A patch difference (4.5.1 against 4.5.3) passes, as does a study with no renv.lock.

Use r_upgrade = TRUE only when you are deliberately moving the study to a new R. The guard then still stops if any package in the lockfile is not installed in this session's library, because the snapshot would drop it; restore those first with renv::restore().

study_need and study_setup call this before they snapshot, so you need to call it yourself only before a snapshot of your own.

Usage

guard_snapshot(
  root,
  r_upgrade = FALSE,
  session = .session_r(),
  installed = .installed_version
)

Arguments

root

Character(1). The study root, holding renv.lock.

r_upgrade

Logical(1). The study is being moved to this session's R on purpose.

session

The R version of this session, a numeric_version. Defaults to the running R; set it only to test the guard.

installed

A function taking a package name and returning its installed version, or NA_character_ when it is not installed. Defaults to a lookup in this session's library; set it only to test the guard.

Value

TRUE, invisibly, when the snapshot may go ahead. Otherwise an error that names both R versions and the R to start.

Examples

root <- tempfile("study")
dir.create(root)
# A study with no renv.lock has nothing to protect:
guard_snapshot(root)

# A lock written by R 4.5.3, checked from a session running R 4.6.1:
writeLines('{"R": {"Version": "4.5.3"}, "Packages": {}}',
           file.path(root, "renv.lock"))
try(guard_snapshot(root, session = numeric_version("4.6.1")))
#> Error : renv.lock records R 4.5.3 but this is R 4.6.1. A snapshot now would record the wrong R and drop packages this R's library lacks. Start R 4.5.3 (/opt/R/4.5.3/bin/R), or pass r_upgrade = TRUE to move the study to R 4.6.1 on purpose.
unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
